diagnoses.preserve: Training custom text-generating networks, configurable architecture, text-dataset input, the few-lines-of-code claim, and the pretrained-model option.
diagnoses.problem: The opening stacks ease and speed promises with the unrestricted claim “any size and complexity.” The page describes configurable architectures but does not establish unlimited scope or consistent ease.
diagnoses.quote: Easily train your own text-generating neural network of any size and complexity on any text dataset with a few lines of code, or quickly train on a text using a pretrained model.

diagnoses.preserve: The introduction to the concrete feature list and the module's technical description.
diagnoses.problem: “Many cool features” adds subjective praise without identifying a capability; the following list already supplies the useful information.

diagnoses.preserve: Attention-weighting, skip-embedding, and their stated training-speed and model-quality purposes.
diagnoses.problem: “Modern” and “new” assert novelty without a date or comparison. These labels add promotional framing to the named architectural techniques.
diagnoses.quote: A modern neural network architecture which utilizes new techniques as attention-weighting and skip-embedding to accelerate training and improve model quality.

diagnoses.preserve: CuDNN RNN implementation, GPU-training condition, and the speed comparison with typical LSTM implementations.
diagnoses.problem: “Powerful” and “massively” amplify the performance claim without a benchmark or stated magnitude.
diagnoses.quote: Utilize a powerful CuDNN implementation of RNNs when trained on the GPU, which massively speeds up training time as opposed to typical LSTM implementations.

diagnoses.preserve: The included model supports training on new texts and can generate text after a single pass; retain the adjacent example and the possibility rather than a guarantee.
diagnoses.problem: “Easily” supplies an unqualified ease claim, while “appropriate text” leaves the quality criterion undefined. The one-pass example supports the workflow but does not define appropriateness.
diagnoses.quote: The included model can easily be trained on new texts, and can generate appropriate text

diagnoses.preserve: The advice to increase temperature for creative output and the adjacent temperature example.
diagnoses.problem: “Significantly” gives no actionable temperature increment or baseline. In the surrounding praise about learning “so well,” it turns useful generation advice into an imprecise performance boast.
diagnoses.quote: that you have to increase the temperature significantly for creative output!)

diagnoses.preserve: Users can influence generation one step at a time, as the next sentence explains through next-character or next-word choices.
diagnoses.problem: This abstract announcement repeats the immediately following operational explanation without adding a condition or capability.
diagnoses.quote: It's also possible to get involved in how the output unfolds, step by step.

diagnoses.preserve: Interactive mode lets users choose among proposed continuations; retain the associated reference.
diagnoses.problem: The prediction about feeling like the writer adds subjective promotional payoff after the selection mechanism has already established user involvement.
diagnoses.quote: to the output; it feels like you're the writer!

diagnoses.preserve: All three layer inputs, temporal weighting and averaging, skip connections from the embeddings and first LSTM, and the stated backpropagation and vanishing-gradient benefits.
diagnoses.problem: A long causal parenthesis embeds a second architectural explanation inside the attention-layer dataflow sentence, making two independently useful mechanisms harder to follow.
diagnoses.quote: All three layers are then fed into an Attention layer to weight the most important temporal features and average them together (and since the embeddings + 1st LSTM are skip-connected into the attention layer, the model updates can backpropagate to them more easily and prevent vanishing gradients).

diagnoses.preserve: The mapping to next-character probabilities, the limit of 394 characters, the vocabulary link, and uppercase, lowercase, punctuation, and emoji coverage.
diagnoses.problem: “That they are the next character” attaches awkwardly to the preceding character count and obscures what the probabilities represent.
diagnoses.quote: that they are the next character in the sequence, including uppercase characters, lowercase, punctuation, and emoji.

diagnoses.preserve: The claimed training and quantitative/qualitative performance benefits of contextual training, with text-only training as the comparison.
diagnoses.problem: “Much faster” asserts an unmeasured magnitude, and “better quantitative and qualitative model performance” names neither metrics nor evaluation criteria. The mechanism is described, but these broad outcome claims are not substantiated on the page.
diagnoses.quote: in all, this results in much faster training and better quantitative and qualitative model performance than just training the model gien the text alone.

diagnoses.preserve: Pretraining is presented as the reason for faster and more accurate fine-tuning.
diagnoses.problem: “Much more robust "knowledge"” uses an intensified metaphor in place of a concrete account of what pretraining contributes; “in the end” adds no defined evaluation point.
diagnoses.quote: However, since the original pretrained network has a much more robust "knowledge" initially, the new textgenrnn trains faster and more accurately in the end,

diagnoses.preserve: The linked character embeddings are presented as carrying contextual information about internet grammar.
diagnoses.problem: “All possible types of modern internet grammar” makes an exhaustive coverage claim that the page does not establish.
diagnoses.quote: include the context for the character for all possible types of modern internet grammar).

diagnoses.preserve: The planned tensorflow.js implementation and the network's small size as its stated advantage.
diagnoses.problem: “Works especially well” does not identify whether small size benefits loading, memory use, execution speed, or another aspect of the planned web implementation.
diagnoses.quote: (works especially well due to the network's small size)

diagnoses.preserve: The plan for a larger pretrained network, support for longer character sequences, and the intended improvement in generated sentences.
diagnoses.problem: “A more indepth understanding of language” substitutes an undefined cognitive metaphor for a model capability, and the sentence presents better output as an assured consequence of a future plan.
diagnoses.quote: A larger pretrained network which can accommodate longer character sequences and a more indepth understanding of language, creating better generated sentences.

diagnoses.preserve: Planned FP16 support for training on Volta/TPUs, conditional on adequate Keras support, and the intended speed benefit.
diagnoses.problem: “Superfast” promises an unspecified speed magnitude for a feature that is still conditional on future support.
diagnoses.quote: FP16 for superfast training on Volta/TPUs (once Keras has good support for it).

diagnoses.preserve: The conditional invitation to support the project through Patreon and appreciation for contributions.
diagnoses.problem: “Good creative use” offers a vague assurance about spending without identifying what donations support beyond the preceding open-source-project statement.
diagnoses.quote: will be put to good creative use.
